chunks: From him, from 'Uthman, from Sama'ah, from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

"Whoever forgets wiping his head, or his feet, or something of the wudu (ablution) that Allah mentioned in the Qur'an, then repeating the wudu (ablution) and the salat (prayer) is obligatory upon him."

key_terms.إِعَادَةُ: repetition or performance again due to invalidity
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), which must also be repeated if based on deficient wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْقُرْآنِ: the Qur'an, cited as the source mentioning these obligatory acts
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification before salat (prayer)
key_terms.رَأْسِهِ: his head, one of the body parts to be wiped in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.قَدَمَيْهِ: his two feet, referred to here as part of the required wiping
key_terms.مَسْحَ: wiping as a required act in wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: What must someone do if they forget part of wudu (ablution), such as wiping the head or feet?
ai.summary: This hadith states that if a person forgets an essential part of wudu (ablution) mentioned by Allah in the Qur'an—such as wiping the head or the feet—then he must repeat both the wudu (ablution) and the salat (prayer). It establishes the legal consequence of omitting a Qur'anically mandated component of ritual purification.
